news.title: EXCLUSIVE: Bibiano Fernandes Opens Up Ahead Of India's U15 FIFA World Cup
news.lede: The Centre for Sports Excellence in Bengaluru is currently brimming with talent. Since August 16, batches of boys have been attending trials for the upcoming FIFA U15 World Cup and Festival 2026. The scouting will see the All India Football Federation (AIFF) shortlist a pool of players who will take part in the next phase of selection. The exercise has become one of the biggest talent hunts Indian football has attempted, and only 14 players will eventually form the 14-member squad which will travel to Azerbaijan for the tournament in October.

news.title: What comes next for Messi after a cruel summer?
news.lede: The 2026 World Cup ended with Argentina losing the final to Spain. Soon after, Lionel Messi returned to Rosario, where he suffered a far greater loss with the death of his father, Jorge. Now, at 39, Messi's future in football is suddenly less certain. A recent report by The Athletic has shed more light on what Messi has been going through since Argentina's 1-0 defeat by Spain in the World Cup final.

news.title: Messi vs Ronaldo: Hat-trick stats compared - who has more?
news.lede: Lionel Messi‘s has scored yet another hat-trick for Inter Miami – but how does he compare to his eternal rival Cristiano Ronaldo when it comes to bagging three goals in a game? The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner netted four in Miami’s 7-1 win over Montreal, showing that age is no barrier to his class. Messi scored his first World Cup hat-trick with all three goals in Argentina’s 3-0 victory over Algeria. The first was a long-range stunner, while the third wasn’t bad either.

news.title: Brazilian World Cup winner Roberto Carlos refutes claims he converted to Islam
news.lede: Brazilian football legend Roberto Carlos, a World Cup winner known for his fearsome free-kicks, has not converted to Islam, contrary to social media posts claiming he had switched religions. Both Carlos and his wife Souhail Al-Tahiri have refuted the claim in separate interviews since the rumours swirled. "Brazil's Roberto Carlos is viewed as the greatest defender of all time.
